//: Markup-fidelity fixture for split-button. CAPABILITY-ONLY (zero scenarios → no render comparison), by the command-palette precedent: the pre-JS SSR shells of the two wrappers diverge in framework-essential ways that are NOT reconcilable into a single golden, so axis-1 (features↔CSS) + axis-2 (features↔maps) completeness is enforced while the render diff is intentionally skipped. See irreconcilableReason. Feature contract authored from dist/css/main.css (pa-btn-split block) + snippets/buttons.html.
irreconcilableReason: The SSR shell differs by LiveView vs client-rendering necessities, not cosmetics: (1) keen's split_button ALWAYS renders id="split-btn-<unique_integer>" + phx-hook="PureAdminSplitButton" (the hook's DOM target) and the empty menu scaffold (<div class="pa-btn-split__menu"><div class="pa-btn-split__menu-inner">) because LiveView renders the menu server-side for the hook to populate; (2) svelte's SplitButton renders NO id, omits data-placement when it equals the default bottom-end, and renders the menu container ONLY when a `menu` snippet is passed (it teleports the menu to <body> on open, client-side). The normalizer keeps id + data-placement (they are not phx-* wiring), so these can't be normalized away, and neither value can be removed without breaking the respective wrapper's runtime. Both are proven aligned on the buttons themselves (same pa-btn / pa-btn--{variant} / pa-btn-split__toggle / pa-btn-split__chevron classes + type="button"; svelte's missing type="button" was FIXED in this slice). The open menu + all items (pa-btn-split__item*, --open, group-label, item-row, in-overflow) are JS-runtime and out of scope regardless (cssStateClasses / cssStateElements).

propsVocabulary.label: primary button label text
propsVocabulary.variant: colour variant applied to BOTH the primary button and the toggle (pa-btn--{variant})

features.//: Feature→class contract authored from dist/css/main.css. variant/size produce pa-btn--* (button.json's block-modifier contract, reused on the split's two buttons). capability.mjs expands + cross-checks against main.css AND each wrapper's map.

variant.note: colours both buttons; pa-btn--{variant} is button.json's contract, reused here

size.note: sizes both buttons; pa-btn--{size} is button.json's contract, reused here

cssStateClasses.//: pa-btn-split--* classes in main.css that are NOT SSR-shell props — toggled by the JS hook at runtime. capability.mjs treats these as legitimately unclaimed.
cssStateClasses.pa-btn-split--open: added by the JS hook while the dropdown is open (rotates the chevron)
cssStateClasses.pa-btn-split--in-overflow: added by overflow.js when a split button is folded into a toolbar's [⋮] more-menu as an atomic group
cssStateClasses.pa-btn-split-chevron-rotate-open: keyframes helper name (not an element class)
cssStateClasses.pa-btn-split-chevron-rotate-closed: keyframes helper name (not an element class)

cssStateElements.//: pa-btn-split__* elements that are either built/populated by the JS hook at runtime or part of the menu scaffold whose SSR presence is wrapper-divergent (keen always, svelte only with a menu slot). Listed so they are not blind spots.
cssStateElements.pa-btn-split__chevron: chevron glyph inside the toggle — present in both shells (aligned), listed for completeness as part of the toggle
cssStateElements.pa-btn-split__toggle: the dropdown toggle button — present in both shells (aligned)
cssStateElements.pa-btn-split__menu: menu container — keen renders it always, svelte only with a menu slot (JS-runtime concern)
cssStateElements.pa-btn-split__menu--open: open-state class the JS hook adds to the menu container when the dropdown opens (svelte's closeMenu/openMenu toggle it)
cssStateElements.pa-btn-split__item: a dropdown menu item — built from the item/menu slot (JS-runtime)
cssStateElements.pa-btn-split__item-icon: leading icon inside a menu item
cssStateElements.pa-btn-split__item-row: wraps a menu item + its inline action button
cssStateElements.pa-btn-split__group-label: section heading overflow.js inserts above a folded atomic group
